lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé has no email address or phone number in the body.
items.because: A recruiter needs a direct way to contact you, and the application may otherwise be discarded.

items.says: The extracted consistency fields for unsupported skills and misspellings are empty or malformed.
items.because: The entries are unusable résumé content and suggest a file or extraction problem.

items.says: Three lines could not be placed cleanly by the parser.
items.because: Another applicant-tracking system may lose or misorder contact details, headings, dates, or bullets.

items.says: The résumé leaves an eight-month period unexplained between the B.A. and the Operations Analyst role.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the gap reflects employment, study, travel, or another activity.

items.says: EDUCATION appears before EXPERIENCE despite four years of professional experience.
items.because: Leading with the MBA makes the résumé read as education-led rather than experience-led.

items.says: Harbor Payments should appear before Crestline Logistics within EXPERIENCE.
items.because: Harbor Payments is more recent and more directly relevant to product work.

items.says: The 35% checkout-conversion improvement lacks a baseline, comparison period, and clarification of relative versus percentage-point change.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the size or credibility of the improvement without that context.

items.says: The dispute self-service bullet does not show what changed after launch.
items.because: Shipping early and defining generic success metrics do not establish that the feature succeeded.

items.says: The queue reduction lacks a starting queue size or a precise period.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the scale of the backlog or the pace of resolution.

items.says: Comparing opt-in and non-opt-in merchants cannot by itself measure the redesign's effect.
items.because: Selection bias and confounding prevent a raw comparison from isolating the redesign's impact.

items.says: The onboarding measurement bullet reports neither the specific metric compared nor its result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether onboarding, conversion, speed, or another metric changed.

items.says: The same onboarding redesign and 2,300-merchant result are attributed to conflicting internship and practicum periods.
items.because: Both entries cannot describe the same intervention occurring in the stated timeframes, which undermines confidence in the dates and ownership.

items.says: The Harbor Payments entry contains several separate workstreams rather than one clear product story.
items.because: Moving among checkout, disputes, chargebacks, tickets, and onboarding makes the contribution harder to scan.

items.says: The standalone onboarding measurement line should be combined with the onboarding result or removed.
items.because: It repeats the onboarding story without reporting a result.

items.says: The late-delivery claim is not a demonstrated reduction in total late deliveries because it excludes weather-delayed shipments.
items.because: Changing the measured population can lower the reported rate without improving delivery performance.

items.says: “Cut warehouse pick errors 30%” is grammatically incomplete because it is missing “by.”
items.because: A percentage reduction requires the standard construction “cut by 30%.”

items.says: The 30% pick-error reduction lacks an error definition, baseline and post-change periods, and comparable denominators.
items.because: Changes in order mix, staffing, volume, or counting rules could otherwise explain the percentage.

items.says: “Coordinated ... and prepares” mixes past and present tense in a role that ended in 2023.
items.because: The mismatch makes it unclear whether the work is current or completed.

items.says: The S&OP review and forecast-pack work has no stated outcome.
items.because: The line reads as task administration rather than showing what the process enabled or changed.

items.says: “S&OP” is unexplained jargon.
items.because: Readers outside operations may not understand what type of meeting was coordinated.

items.says: The claim of saving 1,800 driver hours a year is unsupported by the rollout and training activities alone.
items.because: The figure needs a baseline, calculation method, adoption evidence, and attribution separating the tool from other changes.

items.says: The claim that all 9 tonnes would have been thrown away is an unsupported counterfactual.
items.because: Pickup totals do not by themselves establish that all of the food would otherwise have been discarded.

items.says: The launch bullet does not show how the Product Lead enabled the app launch.
items.because: It gives no product decision, launch mechanism, or feature ownership.

items.says: The volunteer-system bullet does not establish that the system caused the reduction in staff cover shifts.
items.because: The before-and-after figures show association, but staffing demand, operating hours, or reporting practices may also have changed.

items.says: The line repeats the weekly time unit as “each week ... a week.”
The weekly clinic-manager sessions have no resulting change, recommendation, or deliverable.
items.because: The reader cannot see whether the sessions improved scheduling or changed an operating process.

items.says: “Working sessions” is generic wording.
items.because: It makes the activity sound less substantive than it may have been.

items.says: The patient-intake bullet does not establish that front-desk staff adopted the changes.
items.because: Designing the changes does not demonstrate verified usage at the four clinics.

items.says: The bullet gives no size or outcome for shortening the intake form.
items.because: Without fields, pages, minutes, or an improved outcome, the reader cannot gauge the intervention's impact.

items.says: The patient-intake bullet uses passive wording instead of stating the candidate's action.
The merchant-onboarding achievement does not belong under a Regional Hospital Network project.
items.because: Merchant onboarding and first payment are unrelated to the surrounding hospital scheduling and patient-intake work.

items.says: Saying the change “halved” the time is numerically wrong for a reduction from 9 days to 4 days.
items.because: Four days is a reduction of about 55.6%, while half of 9 days is 4.5 days.

items.says: The 2,300-merchant onboarding achievement duplicates the Harbor Payments result.
items.because: Repeating it in both places makes ownership and project relevance unclear.
